definitions.explanation: The most abbreviated and flowing style of Chinese/Japanese calligraphy. Characters are highly simplified and strokes are often connected, making it difficult to read without specialized training.

examples.japanese: {草書|そうしょ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{読|よ}み→読む：00426_yomu⟧にくい。
examples.english: Cursive script is hard to read.

examples.japanese: {草書|そうしょ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{書|か}かれた→書く：00477_kaku⟧⟦{手紙|てがみ}→手紙：00675_tegami⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{解読|かいどく}→解読：14185_kaidoku⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: To decipher a letter written in cursive script.

examples.japanese: ひらがな⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{漢字|かんじ}→漢字：09480_kanji⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{草書|そうしょ}⟦{体|たい}→体：09872_tai⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{生|う}まれた→生まれる：00905_umareru⟧⟦{文字|もじ}→文字：03632_moji⟧だ。
examples.english: Hiragana are characters that evolved from the cursive forms of Chinese characters.

notes: Composed of {草|そう} (grass, rough draft) + ⟦{書|しょ}→〜書：28467_sho⟧ (writing, script). Also called {草書体|そうしょたい}. The most abbreviated of the five script styles. Key historical fact: Japanese hiragana developed from {草書|そうしょ} forms of {万葉仮名|まんようがな} characters — for example, あ derives from the {草書|そうしょ} of {安|あん}, and ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧ from {波|は}. Common collocations: {草書|そうしょ}⟦{体|たい}→体：09872_tai⟧ (cursive style), {草書|そうしょ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧ (to write in cursive). While rarely used in modern daily life, {草書|そうしょ} remains important in ⟦{書道|しょどう}→書道：04178_shodou⟧ (calligraphy) and for reading historical documents.
